en: The Analysis of the Monastic Rules (Bhikkhuvibhaṅga), First Part
Regarding the offenses for one who engages in sexual intercourse, by how many of the seven classes of offenses are those offenses comprised?
The offenses for one who engages in sexual intercourse are comprised by three of the seven classes of offenses.

It may be included in the class of offenses involving defeat (pārājika), it may be included in the class of grave offenses (thullaccaya), or it may be included in the class of offenses of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa)… [and so on]… Regarding one who, out of disrespect, voids excrement, urine, or spittle in water: how many of the seven classes of offenses does this offense fall under?
Regarding one who, out of disrespect, voids excrement, urine, or spittle in water: this offense is included in one of the seven classes of offenses—the class of offenses of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
By the category of offenses of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
The fourth section on inclusion is finished.
